messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT - Latency p95 breach detected for route /v1/generate (smart-routing). Automatic reroute attempted twice. Current state: routing oscillation, some requests hitting fallback region then returning, causing increased tail latency and transient errors. Paging primary on-call: @laura.ops :rotating_light:
laura.ops: I'm on it. Paging history shows two reroutes in last 6m. p50 fine, p95 up ~180ms -> 420ms in bursts. Any recent routing policy changes?
dave.reliability: I saw an ops config push ~9m ago from infra that lowered p95 threshold to 200ms and removed the reroute cooldown (was 5m). That push also introduced a variant-match tweak.
sara-ml: variant-match tweak is the suspicious one — it loosened strict model semantics so a compatible but slower variant (quantized-cpu-fp16) is eligible as fallback. Median okay; fallback variant has worse tail.
kevin-se: customers are reporting slow completions. CS flagged 3 orgs in EU with high error rates. Not full outage but UX degraded.
laura.ops: can we stop automatic reroutes while we investigate? I want to avoid further oscillation.
dave.reliability: doing now — disabling auto_reroute policy for route /v1/generate (api-route-id: rg_09X). Command: `opsctl routing update rg_09X --set auto_reroute=false`
kevin-se: confirmed via dashboard, auto_reroute OFF.
incident-bot: ACTION LOG: auto_reroute disabled by dave.reliability at 1771234570.
laura.ops: good. Next: pin live sessions to current model variants to drain bad variants. Set sticky routing for 10m.
sara-ml: recommended changes: 1) revert variant-match loosen, 2) pin session-level model variant for active sessions, 3) increase p95 reroute threshold to 350ms, 4) reintroduce reroute cooldown to 5m. Proposed quick patch:
```
# quick mitigation config
routing_policy:
  route_id: rg_09X
  auto_reroute: false
  reroute_p95_ms: 350
  reroute_cooldown_s: 300
  session_stickiness_s: 600
  allowed_fallback_variants:
    - llama-2-13b.gz
    # exclude quantized-cpu-fp16 for this route
```
laura.ops: can infra stage that change in prod-safe way? We need to avoid a big rollback.
dave.reliability: I can push a config change to canary group (10% traffic) then promote if sane. But with auto_reroute off, we need to pin existing sessions or they'll hit mismatched population. I'll run a drain job to move new sessions away from cpu fallback variant.
kevin-se: we're seeing a loop pattern: traffic from region-us-east -> region-eu fallback -> back to us-east because cooldown expired quickly. That causes cache misses and increased kv-cache warmup latency.
sara-ml: exact root cause: variant-selection predicate returned true for quantized-cpu-fp16 (faster on cost but worse tail). Combined with aggressive p95 threshold (200ms) and no cooldown, the controller kept bouncing.
laura.ops: make mitigation plan and owner:
- short term (owner: dave.reliability): disable auto_reroute (done), pin sessions, exclude quantized-cpu-fp16 for rg_09X, set reroute threshold 350ms, set cooldown 300s.
- medium term (owner: sara-ml): add canary checks with p95 windowing (5m min) and require >2% traffic for reroute to trigger.
- notify (owner: kevin-se): send customer impact note/PSC.
- postmortem (owner: laura.ops): full timeline + config audit.

dave.reliability: applying exclusion and threshold to canary now. `opsctl routing patch rg_09X --canary=10 --payload-file=canary_patch.yaml`
incident-bot: DEPLOY STARTED canary_patch.yaml by dave.reliability at 1771234584
laura.ops: monitoring canary metrics — p95 for canary down to 210ms after exclusion. No errors on canary.
kevin-se: customer impact: three customers had visible slowdowns; we've opened CS tickets and drafted a status message. No data exfiltration, no auth failures.
sara-ml: note for postmortem: regression came from a config change that widened allowed_variants + lowered thresholds. Two separate low-risk-looking changes combined into a high-risk emergent behavior.
dave.reliability: promoting to 100% in 2m if stable.
incident-bot: DEPLOY SUCCESS canary_patch.yaml promoted to 100% at 1771234592 by dave.reliability
laura.ops: confirmed: global p95 back to ~160-200ms. No further reroutes triggered.
kevin-se: customers notified with interim status. We'll update once postmortem ready.
laura.ops: on-call handoff: I'm handing this to dave.reliability for final verification; I'll stay as incident lead for postmortem. dave - taking over?
dave.reliability: taking over rotation. I'll run the config diff and lock variant-match until we have a safer rollout plan. Also schedule a quick config rollback test in staging.
kevin-se: thumbs up. Any follow-ups for product or security?
sara-ml: product: add a change control step when altering fallback variant sets. Security: nothing immediate.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation applied, auto_reroute remains disabled until postmortem and policy adjustments completed. Severity: Sev3 -> monitoring. Incident timeline recorded.
laura.ops: OK to close this thread after an initial writeup? I will create the postmortem doc and link to channel.
dave.reliability: will verify stability for 24h and then close.
pagerduty: Incident acknowledged and marked resolved for paging (no more alerts).
laura.ops: thanks everyone. Postmortem owners: laura.ops (lead), sara-ml (root cause), dave.reliability (mitigation), kevin-se (customer comms).
